# Find the Distance Value Between Two Arrays.

@example 12 is exactly 3 away from 15, so it does not count; 3 and -6 are more than 3 away from both 7 and 15.
[3,12,-6]
[7,15]
3
=> 2

@example With d = 0 only an equal value is too close: 5 matches, and each of the two 0s counts.
[0,0,5]
[5]
0
=> 2

@example 20 is exactly 10 away from 30, and -20 from -30, so neither counts.
[20,-20]
[-30,30,0]
10
=> 0

# Smallest inputs: one equal entry each, d = 0.
[1]
[1]
0
=> 0

# A gap of d + 1 below and above keeps clear...
[50]
[40,60]
9
=> 1

# ...a gap of exactly d, on either side, does not.
[50]
[40,60]
10
=> 0

# The close entry of arr2 is just below 10 for the first entry, just above
# 25 for the second; 33 keeps clear. Looking only at the first arr2 entry
# at or above x, or only at the one before it, misses one of them.
[10,25,33]
[9,27,40]
2
=> 1

# Entries below all of arr2 and above all of it keep clear; 1 does not.
[-500,500,1]
[0,1,2]
100
=> 2

# Repeated values in arr1: each clear copy counts (the 2s), close ones
# don't (the 7s). arr2 has a repeat too.
[7,7,7,2,2]
[5,5]
2
=> 2

# The first entry is close and the rest keep clear: counting must go on.
[1,100,200]
[1]
0
=> 2

# Negative values and both signs: no value matches, so with d = 0 all
# four keep clear...
[-3,-1,2,4]
[-2,3]
0
=> 4

# ...but each is 1 away from an arr2 entry, so with d = 1 none does.
[-3,-1,2,4]
[-2,3]
1
=> 0

# Every value equal.
[5,5,5]
[5,5]
100
=> 0

# The ends of the range with d = 100: -1000 is 101 away from -899 and keeps
# clear; 1000 is exactly 100 away from 900.
[-1000,1000]
[-899,900]
100
=> 1

# Windows that reach past -1000 and 1000, with nothing in them.
[1000,-1000,999,-999]
[0]
100
=> 4

# arr2 holds the two ends of the range: 940 is exactly 60 below 1000 and
# -960 is 40 above -1000, so only 0 keeps clear. A window clipped to
# -999..999 (an off-by-one at either end) misses them.
[940,-960,0]
[1000,-1000]
60
=> 1

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
[-6,-2,-7,-5,-1,6,-1]
[-5,1,-4,-6,1,5,-7]
3
=> 0

@gen 2 small
[-976,949,-931,-989,-882]
[956,-932,946,-887,924]
100
=> 0

@gen 3 small
[1000,1000,912,941,998,-880,973,-956]
[1000,-975,953]
90
=> 1

@gen 4 small
[-6,4,4,5]
[8,2,-7]
0
=> 4

@gen 5 small
[-4,8,1,8,-8,2]
[-7,5]
2
=> 5

@gen 6 small
[0,3]
[-5,-2]
1
=> 2

@gen 7 small
[-8,-7,6,-6,-8,6]
[4,-3,-7,-8,-4,-7,-2]
0
=> 3
